pm8_frontmatter.title: Adipose Endocrine Regulation
pm8_frontmatter.mission: Regulate adipose-derived endocrine signalling and local glucocorticoid responsiveness to communicate metabolic state and coordinate hormonal adaptation.
pm8_frontmatter.summary: Adipose tissue releases hormones that communicate metabolic state. Adipokine output and local glucocorticoid responsiveness are regulated processes whose measured endpoints must be distinguished.
cofactors: NADPH — biochemical reducing equivalent for 11β-HSD1; no dietary admission inferred
pm8_frontmatter.dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipokine responses depend on hormone, depot and exposure
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Insulin and glucocorticoid exposures regulate leptin synthesis or release and adiponectin expression or release in human adipose preparations, with context-dependent responses.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Insulin and glucocorticoid exposures regulate leptin synthesis or release and adiponectin expression or release in human adipose preparations, with context-dependent responses.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Human adipose pulse-labelling separates leptin biosynthesis from release of stored protein. Dexamethasone can increase leptin synthesis while suppressing adiponectin release in other preparations; these are distinct hormone-specific responses. Circulating adiponectin responses to systemic glucocorticoids are not uniformly reproduced.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human adipose pulse-labelling separates leptin biosynthesis from release of stored protein. Dexamethasone can increase leptin synthesis while suppressing adiponectin release in other preparations; these are distinct hormone-specific responses. Circulating adiponectin responses to systemic glucocorticoids are not uniformly reproduced.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Ex vivo hormone exposures and pharmacological glucocorticoids do not establish ordinary dietary effects. Donor adiposity, depot, exposure duration and concentration matter; circulating concentrations do not measure secretion rates or receptor sensitivity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Local adipose cortisol regeneration differs from systemic metabolism
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human adipose cortisol regeneration is tissue- and metabolic-context dependent; whole-body dietary changes in cortisol metabolism do not necessarily alter subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human adipose cortisol regeneration is tissue- and metabolic-context dependent; whole-body dietary changes in cortisol metabolism do not necessarily alter subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Microdialysis and tracer measurements distinguish local cortisone-to-cortisol conversion from systemic turnover. Insulin effects differed by adiposity. A low-carbohydrate crossover altered systemic cortisol metabolism without a measured adipose 11β-HSD1 response; weight loss in another small study increased adipocyte transcript expression rather than demonstrating universal suppression.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Microdialysis and tracer measurements distinguish local cortisone-to-cortisol conversion from systemic turnover. Insulin effects differed by adiposity. A low-carbohydrate crossover altered systemic cortisol metabolism without a measured adipose 11β-HSD1 response; weight loss in another small study increased adipocyte transcript expression rather than demonstrating universal suppression.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Small selected samples and differing assays; transcript abundance is not in vivo regeneration flux. Systemic or hepatic effects cannot be assigned to adipose, and less local cortisol activity is not assumed universally beneficial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipocyte glucocorticoid-receptor reduction changes mouse stress feedback
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Reducing glucocorticoid-receptor expression in adiponectin-Cre mice increased restraint-related corticosterone responses and impaired dexamethasone feedback, without a detected baseline leptin or adiponectin difference.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Reducing glucocorticoid-receptor expression in adiponectin-Cre mice increased restraint-related corticosterone responses and impaired dexamethasone feedback, without a detected baseline leptin or adiponectin difference.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The genetic experiment supports a qualified contribution of adipocyte-enriched GR signalling to mouse stress feedback. The communicating signal was not identified; unchanged baseline adipokines do not establish an adipokine-mediated pathway. Human stress feedback through the same route remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The genetic experiment supports a qualified contribution of adipocyte-enriched GR signalling to mouse stress feedback. The communicating signal was not identified; unchanged baseline adipokines do not establish an adipokine-mediated pathway. Human stress feedback through the same route remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Genetic mouse model, incomplete and depot-variable knockdown, possible untested off-target sites, and developmental effects. Baseline hormone concentrations do not exclude dynamic secretion changes. No human dietary, cognitive or ADHD effect is established.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Diet and activity outcomes distinguish circulating hormones from local production
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dietary energy restriction and physical activity can change selected circulating adipokines or adipose transcripts, but these endpoints do not establish a uniform change in adipokine secretion or improved endocrine responsiveness.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Dietary energy restriction and physical activity can change selected circulating adipokines or adipose transcripts, but these endpoints do not establish a uniform change in adipokine secretion or improved endocrine responsiveness.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Alternate-day and daily energy restriction reduced circulating leptin without an adiponectin change in one randomised trial. POUNDS Lost reported increased circulating adiponectin over two years across diet groups. A small walking trial increased adipose adiponectin mRNA without a significant plasma increase. Duration, tissue measurement and circulating exposure must remain separate.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Alternate-day and daily energy restriction reduced circulating leptin without an adiponectin change in one randomised trial. POUNDS Lost reported increased circulating adiponectin over two years across diet groups. A small walking trial increased adipose adiponectin mRNA without a significant plasma increase. Duration, tissue measurement and circulating exposure must remain separate.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: These trials do not directly quantify adipose secretion or receptor sensitivity. Lower leptin or higher adiponectin is not automatically a better endocrine state. Selected populations, adherence and weight change limit translation; no optimal universal protocol or brain outcome is established.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: Moderate weight loss improved insulin action before the measured adipose inflammatory markers declined.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Moderate weight loss improved insulin action before the measured adipose inflammatory markers declined.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Early metabolic improvement did not require a detectable reduction in the measured subcutaneous inflammatory markers; greater losses were accompanied by further tissue changes.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Early metabolic improvement did not require a detectable reduction in the measured subcutaneous inflammatory markers; greater losses were accompanied by further tissue changes.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Later progressive-loss comparisons involved nine participants and were not independently randomized; other depots and unmeasured inflammatory processes remain uncertain.

evidence_considered.label: Magkos et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: At 5% loss insulin sensitivity improved without reduced measured systemic or subcutaneous inflammation; greater loss altered oxidative-stress, matrix and inflammatory pathways.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Weight maintenance versus initial 5% diet-induced loss; later approximately 11% and 16% loss with abdominal subcutaneous biopsy and tracer/clamp measurements.
evidence_considered.study_finding: At 5% loss insulin sensitivity improved without reduced measured systemic or subcutaneous inflammation; greater loss altered oxidative-stress, matrix and inflammatory pathways.

assessment.study: Weight maintenance versus initial 5% diet-induced loss; later approximately 11% and 16% loss with abdominal subcutaneous biopsy and tracer/clamp measurements.
assessment.population: 40 adults with obesity and insulin resistance randomized; 33 completed the initial comparison and nine continued progressive loss.
assessment.result: At 5% loss insulin sensitivity improved without reduced measured systemic or subcutaneous inflammation; greater loss altered oxidative-stress, matrix and inflammatory pathways.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Actual losses 5.1%, 10.8% and 16.4%; no pooled inflammatory effect or universal threshold estimated.
assessment.evidence_summary: At 5% loss insulin sensitivity improved without reduced measured systemic or subcutaneous inflammation; greater loss altered oxidative-stress, matrix and inflammatory pathways.
assessment.limitations: Attrition and selected later subgroup; endpoint timing and depot specificity prevent universal mediation claims.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full text: Methods, Results, Tables 1–4, tissue expression results and Discussion.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Mohammad & Thiemermann (2021)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews a possible gut LPS/TLR4 route into metabolic inflammation.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Review evidence and endotoxin assay limitations do not isolate a food-to-adipose intervention; the route is contextual.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Cazzola et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Review of magnesium and adipose stress; primary candidate follow-up is assessed in PM8-F8.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Not an independent experiment or evidence that extra dietary magnesium reduces human adipose inflammation.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Di Girolamo et al. (2022)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Provides clinical metabolic-comorbidity context rather than an adipose intervention.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not measure a dietary intervention on adipose stress or establish a PM-to-Phenome causal relationship.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Marcelli et al. (2025)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Provides clinical metabolic-comorbidity context rather than an adipose intervention.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not measure a dietary intervention on adipose stress or establish a PM-to-Phenome causal relationship.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Blood-cell cytokines do not identify an adipose source
scientific_findings.finding_summary: EPA-rich supplementation lowered stimulated immune-cell IL-6 production in medical students.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: EPA-rich supplementation lowered stimulated immune-cell IL-6 production in medical students.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This source supports an immune-cell effect, while adipose-specific evidence is assessed separately in PM8-F6.
scientific_findings.synthesis: This source supports an immune-cell effect, while adipose-specific evidence is assessed separately in PM8-F6.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: No adipose biopsy or adipose-specific endpoint; anxiety results cannot be attributed to adipose mediation.

evidence_considered.label: Kiecolt-Glaser et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Stimulated IL-6 production was lower in the supplement group.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Double-blind 12-week randomized comparison of 2.5 g/day omega-3 supplement (2085 mg EPA and 348 mg DHA) versus placebo.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Stimulated IL-6 production was lower in the supplement group.

assessment.study: Double-blind 12-week randomized comparison of 2.5 g/day omega-3 supplement (2085 mg EPA and 348 mg DHA) versus placebo.
assessment.population: 68 medical students.
assessment.result: Stimulated IL-6 production was lower in the supplement group.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 14% lower LPS-stimulated IL-6 production versus controls.
assessment.evidence_summary: Stimulated IL-6 production was lower in the supplement group.
assessment.limitations: A peripheral immune-cell assay cannot locate inflammation in adipose tissue.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full-text abstract, exposure and outcome definitions.

scientific_findings.finding_label: A defined green Mediterranean pattern reduced visceral fat
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The green Mediterranean diet package reduced MRI-measured visceral fat more than the comparison diets in DIRECT-PLUS.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The green Mediterranean diet package reduced MRI-measured visceral fat more than the comparison diets in DIRECT-PLUS.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The pattern is a dietary target for visceral adiposity; its individual foods remain candidates for component-specific testing. Related circulating-protein changes strengthen relevance to metabolic inflammation without proving adipose mediation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The pattern is a dietary target for visceral adiposity; its individual foods remain candidates for component-specific testing. Related circulating-protein changes strengthen relevance to metabolic inflammation without proving adipose mediation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: One predominantly male workplace cohort; the foods were not independently randomized, fat volume is not a biopsy of inflammation, and the protein analysis is not independent replication.

evidence_considered.label: Zelicha et al. (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Green-MED produced greater visceral-fat reduction.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 18-month healthy dietary guidance, Mediterranean or green-Mediterranean programme, all with physical activity; both MED groups received 28 g/day walnuts; green-MED added 3–4 cups/day green tea, 100 g/day frozen Mankai and reduced red/processed meat.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Green-MED produced greater visceral-fat reduction.

assessment.study: 18-month healthy dietary guidance, Mediterranean or green-Mediterranean programme, all with physical activity; both MED groups received 28 g/day walnuts; green-MED added 3–4 cups/day green tea, 100 g/day frozen Mankai and reduced red/processed meat.
assessment.population: 294 randomized adults with abdominal obesity/dyslipidaemia; 88% men; 79.3% had eligible follow-up MRI.
assessment.result: Green-MED produced greater visceral-fat reduction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: VAT change −14.1% green-MED, −6.0% MED, −4.2% guidance; weight-adjusted green-MED versus MED p=0.042, versus guidance p=0.07.
assessment.evidence_summary: Green-MED produced greater visceral-fat reduction.
assessment.limitations: Open-label package, incomplete MRI follow-up and post-randomization adjustment; no isolated food attribution or adipose inflammatory mediation.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full text: allocation, exposures, MRI, results and adjusted comparisons; funding includes California Walnuts Commission.

evidence_considered.label: Zelicha et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: MED diets changed inflammation-related circulating proteins; green-MED showed more pronounced changes, with protein-cluster changes correlated with VAT reduction.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Olink circulating-protein panels across the dietary intervention.
evidence_considered.study_finding: MED diets changed inflammation-related circulating proteins; green-MED showed more pronounced changes, with protein-cluster changes correlated with VAT reduction.

assessment.study: Olink circulating-protein panels across the dietary intervention.
assessment.population: DIRECT-PLUS participants: the same randomized cohort as the 2022 VAT report.
assessment.result: MED diets changed inflammation-related circulating proteins; green-MED showed more pronounced changes, with protein-cluster changes correlated with VAT reduction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported adjusted p<0.05 for selected protein changes; no tissue-specific mediated effect quantified.
assessment.evidence_summary: MED diets changed inflammation-related circulating proteins; green-MED showed more pronounced changes, with protein-cluster changes correlated with VAT reduction.
assessment.limitations: Secondary proteomics, multiplicity and same-cohort dependency; circulating proteins do not establish adipose origin.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Willmann et al. (2019)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: A separate six-month randomized dietary study compared reduced red meat and increased fibre within calorie restriction; visceral fat fell in all groups.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: No additional cardiometabolic advantage of the food changes was established in that context; it does not isolate which green-MED component explains its package result.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Park et al. (2014)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: A different pomegranate-vinegar formulation showed a preliminary CT-measured visceral-fat signal in overweight women.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Publisher-indexed abstract/result only was recovered; this is a vinegar-plus-extract formulation, not pomegranate fruit or a DIRECT-PLUS intervention. Independent efficacy and formulation details remain unresolved.

evidence_dependency: The 2022 VAT and 2024 proteome publications analyse DIRECT-PLUS (NCT03020186); count one intervention cohort, not two replications. PM8-F4 reuses the 2022 study for component attribution, not an independent food trial.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: The green-MED trial identifies walnuts as a food candidate, but does not isolate a walnut-specific effect on visceral fat.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The green-MED trial identifies walnuts as a food candidate, but does not isolate a walnut-specific effect on visceral fat.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: A separate walnut trial was null for visceral fat. A newer walnut-based low-carbohydrate trial reported a favourable change interaction, but changed macronutrients as well; component causality remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A separate walnut trial was null for visceral fat. A newer walnut-based low-carbohydrate trial reported a favourable change interaction, but changed macronutrients as well; component causality remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Different diet packages, fat measurement methods and statistical contrasts cannot establish a stand-alone walnut dose or identify ellagitannins as the active ingredient.

evidence_considered.label: Njike et al. (2015)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: No significant effect on visceral fat or the reported anthropometric measures.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Randomized walnut-included (56 g/day) and walnut-excluded dietary periods of six months, with or without calorie-adjustment advice.
evidence_considered.study_finding: No significant effect on visceral fat or the reported anthropometric measures.

assessment.study: Randomized walnut-included (56 g/day) and walnut-excluded dietary periods of six months, with or without calorie-adjustment advice.
assessment.population: 112 adults at risk for diabetes.
assessment.result: No significant effect on visceral fat or the reported anthropometric measures.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No significant visceral-fat difference; a precise interval for this endpoint was not recovered.
assessment.evidence_summary: No significant effect on visceral fat or the reported anthropometric measures.
assessment.limitations: Null result bounds an efficacy claim; it is not proof that every walnut substitution has no effect.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary journal abstract/results and body-composition findings.

evidence_considered.label: Dong et al. (2026)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: VFA group-by-time interaction favoured the walnut-based diet; endpoint group comparison was nonsignificant.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week randomized walnut-based low-carbohydrate versus high-carbohydrate low-fat diet; 150 g/day refers to replaced staple food, not walnut dose.
evidence_considered.study_finding: VFA group-by-time interaction favoured the walnut-based diet; endpoint group comparison was nonsignificant.

assessment.study: 12-week randomized walnut-based low-carbohydrate versus high-carbohydrate low-fat diet; 150 g/day refers to replaced staple food, not walnut dose.
assessment.population: Adults with central obesity; exact sample and walnut gram dose not independently recovered in this assessment.
assessment.result: VFA group-by-time interaction favoured the walnut-based diet; endpoint group comparison was nonsignificant.
assessment.effect_magnitude: VFA interaction p=0.014; no significant between-group VFA difference at week 12.
assessment.evidence_summary: VFA group-by-time interaction favoured the walnut-based diet; endpoint group comparison was nonsignificant.
assessment.limitations: Abstract-only recovery; combined macronutrient substitution prevents attribution to walnuts alone.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Zelicha et al. (2022)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Walnuts were supplied to both MED groups, and intake was associated with VAT loss.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The food association is not an independently randomized walnut effect; the package result is assessed in PM8-F3.

evidence_dependency: DIRECT-PLUS component associations reuse PM8-F3 evidence; Njike and Dong are separate trials, but test different exposures.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Tea beverage results depend on formulation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Some catechin-enriched tea beverages reduced visceral fat, while a newer catechin-plus-inulin beverage did not.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Some catechin-enriched tea beverages reduced visceral fat, while a newer catechin-plus-inulin beverage did not.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Green tea is a reasonable component to test, with evidence tied to the actual beverage and comparator. Ordinary brewed tea, catechin-enriched products and combined formulations are not equivalent exposures.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Green tea is a reasonable component to test, with evidence tied to the actual beverage and comparator. Ordinary brewed tea, catechin-enriched products and combined formulations are not equivalent exposures.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The positive and null trials differ in formulation, population and fat assessment; neither isolates adipose inflammatory signalling or proves a general brewed-tea effect.

evidence_considered.label: Nagao et al. (2007)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The higher-catechin group had greater reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat area.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week double-blind comparison of tea beverages with 583 versus 96 mg catechins/day, maintaining usual diet/activity.
evidence_considered.study_finding: The higher-catechin group had greater reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat area.

assessment.study: 12-week double-blind comparison of tea beverages with 583 versus 96 mg catechins/day, maintaining usual diet/activity.
assessment.population: Japanese adults with visceral-fat-type obesity; 240 per-protocol participants.
assessment.result: The higher-catechin group had greater reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat area.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Direction significant as reported; precise between-group VAT estimate and interval not recovered.
assessment.evidence_summary: The higher-catechin group had greater reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat area.
assessment.limitations: Per-protocol analysis, enriched beverage and manufacturer affiliation limit transfer to ordinary brewed tea.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

evidence_considered.label: Iino et al. (2026)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Visceral-fat area did not differ significantly, despite an improvement in HOMA-IR.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week double-blind placebo-controlled catechin 400 mg/day plus inulin 2.3 g/day beverage.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Visceral-fat area did not differ significantly, despite an improvement in HOMA-IR.

assessment.study: 12-week double-blind placebo-controlled catechin 400 mg/day plus inulin 2.3 g/day beverage.
assessment.population: 96 randomized Japanese adults with visceral obesity; 91 in primary full-analysis set.
assessment.result: Visceral-fat area did not differ significantly, despite an improvement in HOMA-IR.
assessment.effect_magnitude: VFA change +0.91 versus +4.61 cm²; p=0.243.
assessment.evidence_summary: Visceral-fat area did not differ significantly, despite an improvement in HOMA-IR.
assessment.limitations: Combined formulation and bioimpedance VFA; neither positive insulin result nor null fat result isolates tea alone.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Marine omega-3 tissue effects vary with context
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Marine omega-3 formulations can change adipose inflammatory endpoints, but effects differ across populations and assays.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Marine omega-3 formulations can change adipose inflammatory endpoints, but effects differ across populations and assays.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Biopsy evidence is mixed: Spencer found lower macrophage/MCP-1 endpoints, Hames did not replicate a tissue inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation, and Fisk found limited responses in obesity. A conditional formulation-specific practice remains provisional rather than a reliable general treatment.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Biopsy evidence is mixed: Spencer found lower macrophage/MCP-1 endpoints, Hames did not replicate a tissue inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation, and Fisk found limited responses in obesity. A conditional formulation-specific practice remains provisional rather than a reliable general treatment.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Doses, baseline metabolic state, depot and assays differ; tissue target engagement does not establish improved insulin sensitivity or an ordinary-food equivalent.

evidence_considered.label: Spencer et al. (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Adipose macrophages and MCP-1 decreased; capillaries increased; insulin sensitivity did not change.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week placebo-controlled 4 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl ester formulation with adipose biopsies.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Adipose macrophages and MCP-1 decreased; capillaries increased; insulin sensitivity did not change.

assessment.study: 12-week placebo-controlled 4 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl ester formulation with adipose biopsies.
assessment.population: Insulin-resistant adults without diabetes.
assessment.result: Adipose macrophages and MCP-1 decreased; capillaries increased; insulin sensitivity did not change.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported direction; no harmonized between-trial tissue effect estimate calculated.
assessment.evidence_summary: Adipose macrophages and MCP-1 decreased; capillaries increased; insulin sensitivity did not change.
assessment.limitations: Selected population and high-dose ethyl ester formulation; no isolated EPA versus DHA effect.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

evidence_considered.label: Fisk et al. (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Inflammatory transcriptome and oxylipin responses were more limited in participants with obesity.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week double-blind fish-oil concentrate (1.1 g EPA + 0.8 g DHA/day) versus corn oil with subcutaneous biopsies.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Inflammatory transcriptome and oxylipin responses were more limited in participants with obesity.

assessment.study: 12-week double-blind fish-oil concentrate (1.1 g EPA + 0.8 g DHA/day) versus corn oil with subcutaneous biopsies.
assessment.population: 45 adults with obesity and 39 normal-weight adults.
assessment.result: Inflammatory transcriptome and oxylipin responses were more limited in participants with obesity.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No common pooled estimate; results are endpoint- and population-specific.
assessment.evidence_summary: Inflammatory transcriptome and oxylipin responses were more limited in participants with obesity.
assessment.limitations: Cross-population baseline differences and molecular endpoints prevent a uniform efficacy claim.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Indexed primary full-text Summary, Methods and population characteristics; detailed transcript/oxylipin tables not reanalysed.

evidence_considered.label: Hames et al. (2017)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: EPA/DHA incorporation increased, without improved measured adipose inflammation or insulin regulation of lipolysis.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Six-month randomized double-blind omega-3 formulation versus oleate placebo.
evidence_considered.study_finding: No measured tissue benefit despite increased EPA/DHA content.

assessment.study: Six-month double-blind placebo-controlled trial; 3.9 g/day EPA+DHA (4.2 g total omega-3) versus 4.2 g/day oleate.
assessment.population: Insulin-resistant adults with overweight or obesity; 12 supplement and nine placebo completers in the adipose substudy.
assessment.result: Adipose EPA/DHA increased, but macrophage content, crown-like structures, senescent cells and insulin regulation of lipolysis did not improve.
assessment.effect_magnitude: CD68 macrophages 31 to 33 per 100 adipocytes with omega-3 versus 33 to 31 with placebo; interaction p=0.25; lipolysis suppression interaction p=0.11.
assessment.evidence_summary: Tissue delivery was demonstrated without the expected inflammatory or lipolytic benefit.
assessment.limitations: Small completer substudy, baseline phenotype differences and subcutaneous-only sampling; not proof of no effect in every metabolic context.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full-text Methods, Results, Tables 1–2 and Discussion.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipose stress includes immune and oxidative processes
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Adipose expansion is associated with macrophage inflammatory activity, while acute overnutrition can impair metabolism before measured cytokines rise.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Adipose expansion is associated with macrophage inflammatory activity, while acute overnutrition can impair metabolism before measured cytokines rise.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Macrophage recruitment and oxidative stress provide complementary biological routes; reducing fat mass or a blood cytokine cannot be treated as a complete assay of either route.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Macrophage recruitment and oxidative stress provide complementary biological routes; reducing fat mass or a blood cytokine cannot be treated as a complete assay of either route.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Human macrophage evidence includes observational associations; extreme acute overfeeding in six men is not an ordinary-diet experiment or proof of a universal sequence.

evidence_considered.label: Weisberg et al. (2003)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Adipocyte size and adiposity tracked macrophage accumulation; macrophages contributed inflammatory gene expression.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Expression profiling, histology and cell-fraction analyses across adiposity.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Adipocyte size and adiposity tracked macrophage accumulation; macrophages contributed inflammatory gene expression.

assessment.study: Expression profiling, histology and cell-fraction analyses across adiposity.
assessment.population: Mouse obesity models and human subcutaneous adipose samples.
assessment.result: Adipocyte size and adiposity tracked macrophage accumulation; macrophages contributed inflammatory gene expression.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Directional histological and molecular evidence; no dietary effect size inferred.
assessment.evidence_summary: Adipocyte size and adiposity tracked macrophage accumulation; macrophages contributed inflammatory gene expression.
assessment.limitations: Mixed species; human associations do not prove macrophage mediation in every obesity phenotype.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

evidence_considered.label: Boden et al. (2015)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Oxidative stress and insulin resistance developed without initial increases in the measured inflammatory cytokines.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Short-term extreme overfeeding at about 2–2.5 times habitual calories with adipose and metabolic measures.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Oxidative stress and insulin resistance developed without initial increases in the measured inflammatory cytokines.

assessment.study: Short-term extreme overfeeding at about 2–2.5 times habitual calories with adipose and metabolic measures.
assessment.population: Six healthy non-obese men.
assessment.result: Oxidative stress and insulin resistance developed without initial increases in the measured inflammatory cytokines.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Mechanistic direction retained; no usual-diet dose or food-specific estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Oxidative stress and insulin resistance developed without initial increases in the measured inflammatory cytokines.
assessment.limitations: Small acute challenge with major energy excess; oxidative association does not establish every causal step.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and indexed study results; full methods not independently recovered.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Magnesium is a research candidate with context-dependent adipose effects
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A simple claim that more magnesium reduces adipose stress is not established by the assessed evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: A simple claim that more magnesium reduces adipose stress is not established by the assessed evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The attached review motivates investigation; primary mouse data show that low-magnesium exposure can reduce fat accumulation while raising circulating lipids. This challenges a simple adiposity-as-benefit interpretation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The attached review motivates investigation; primary mouse data show that low-magnesium exposure can reduce fat accumulation while raising circulating lipids. This challenges a simple adiposity-as-benefit interpretation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Mouse deficiency is not a human dietary strategy; a PM8-specific human dependency or tissue benefit remains unresolved after targeted retrieval.

evidence_considered.label: Kurstjens et al. (2018)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Low magnesium reduced high-fat-induced obesity and altered adipose lipolysis, while blood lipids remained high.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: 17-week low- versus normal-magnesium diets crossed with low- or high-fat feeding.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Low magnesium reduced high-fat-induced obesity and altered adipose lipolysis, while blood lipids remained high.

assessment.study: 17-week low- versus normal-magnesium diets crossed with low- or high-fat feeding.
assessment.population: Male mice, approximately 12 per diet group, plus a replication experiment.
assessment.result: Low magnesium reduced high-fat-induced obesity and altered adipose lipolysis, while blood lipids remained high.
assessment.effect_magnitude: High-fat group body weights approximately 47.0 versus 38.6 g, normal versus low magnesium; p<0.05.
assessment.evidence_summary: Low magnesium reduced high-fat-induced obesity and altered adipose lipolysis, while blood lipids remained high.
assessment.limitations: Animal-only severe deficiency, not a human adequacy comparison; smaller fat mass is not proof of healthier adipose signalling.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full-text Abstract, Methods, Results and lipid/adipose outcomes.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Cazzola et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Attached narrative review covers magnesium, oxidative stress and adipose physiology.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Review is a discovery source; its qualitative biology does not establish human PM8 dietary efficacy.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Exercise can remodel adipose tissue without weight loss
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Exercise training altered subcutaneous adipose structure without weight loss in adults with obesity.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Exercise training altered subcutaneous adipose structure without weight loss in adults with obesity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Regular activity is relevant to adipose remodelling, but the observed signalling changes are not a blanket reduction in inflammation or proof that one training intensity is superior.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Regular activity is relevant to adipose remodelling, but the observed signalling changes are not a blanket reduction in inflammation or proof that one training intensity is superior.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Counterbalanced allocation between two exercise programmes, no sedentary control and several transient responses limit causal and durability claims.

evidence_considered.study_exposure: 12-week continuous moderate-intensity or interval training, four days/week; weight maintained; biopsies one and four days after final session.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Adipocyte size, matrix and capillarization changed; several molecular responses reversed after four days.

assessment.result: Adipocyte size, matrix and capillarization changed; several molecular responses reversed after four days.

assessment.evidence_summary: Adipocyte size, matrix and capillarization changed; several molecular responses reversed after four days.

assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary indexed Methods, allocation and Discussion recovered.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Sleep restriction can promote visceral-fat accumulation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Severe sleep restriction increased visceral fat during a controlled experiment with freely available food.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Severe sleep restriction increased visceral fat during a controlled experiment with freely available food.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Avoiding repeated severe sleep loss is relevant to adipose load. This experiment does not establish that sleep extension reverses established adipose inflammation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Avoiding repeated severe sleep loss is relevant to adipose load. This experiment does not establish that sleep extension reverses established adipose inflammation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Small young, predominantly male sample, severe imposed restriction and ad-libitum intake; no adipose inflammatory biopsy.

evidence_considered.label: Covassin et al. (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Sleep restriction increased energy intake and abdominal visceral-fat accumulation.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Randomized inpatient crossover, 14 days of four- versus nine-hour sleep opportunity within 21-day periods.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Sleep restriction increased energy intake and abdominal visceral-fat accumulation.

assessment.study: Randomized inpatient crossover, 14 days of four- versus nine-hour sleep opportunity within 21-day periods.
assessment.population: 12 healthy non-obese adults, nine men, aged 19–39.
assessment.result: Sleep restriction increased energy intake and abdominal visceral-fat accumulation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 11% VAT accumulation and approximately 308 kcal/day greater intake versus control.
assessment.evidence_summary: Sleep restriction increased energy intake and abdominal visceral-fat accumulation.
assessment.limitations: Sleep loss and increased intake act together; not a calorie-matched or sleep-extension reversal trial.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary journal Methods, Discussion and central illustration.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Time-restricted eating has context-specific adipose findings
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Time-restricted eating showed exploratory adipose pathway changes in TREAD, but another trial found no extra visceral-fat reduction over Mediterranean-diet education.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Time-restricted eating showed exploratory adipose pathway changes in TREAD, but another trial found no extra visceral-fat reduction over Mediterranean-diet education.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The 10-hour protocol is a provisional practice for adults with obesity and long baseline eating windows; its tissue mechanism remains exploratory.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The 10-hour protocol is a provisional practice for adults with obesity and long baseline eating windows; its tissue mechanism remains exploratory.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: TREAD selected the greatest weight losers for RNA-seq, and fat endpoints and populations differed across trials; timing-independent anti-inflammatory benefit is unproven.

evidence_considered.label: Wilkinson et al. (2026)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Weight loss favoured TRE; inflammatory gene-set signals decreased in the selected biopsy subgroup.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Reduces visceral adipose volume in the tested weight-loss programme, with associated changes in circulating inflammation-related proteins.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Green Mediterranean dietary pattern
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: This tested pattern combined walnuts (28 g/day), green tea (3–4 cups/day), Mankai (100 g/day frozen plant in a shake), and reduced red/processed meat. It reduced visceral fat more than the comparison diets in adults with abdominal obesity. These foods are targets for further testing: their individual contributions remain uncertain, walnut evidence is mixed, and enriched tea beverages are not interchangeable with ordinary brewed tea.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: Progressive diet-induced loss altered subcutaneous adipose tissue pathways; moderate initial loss improved insulin action before measured inflammation declined.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Later progressive-loss comparisons involved nine participants and were not independently randomized; other depots and unmeasured inflammatory processes remain uncertain.
system_optimisation_practices.reader_description: A diet-induced weight-reduction programme changed adipose tissue biology in adults with obesity. Early insulin improvements preceded the measured inflammatory decline, and later tissue comparisons were small.
system_optimisation_practices.dietary_input_note: Dietary energy-reduction programme; not a universal weight-loss prescription.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Marine omega-3 formulations in selected metabolic contexts

system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Doses, baseline metabolic state, depot and assays differ; tissue target engagement does not establish improved insulin sensitivity or an ordinary-food equivalent.
system_optimisation_practices.dietary_input_note: Supplement exposure only; no ordinary-food dose or walnut-ALA equivalence established.
system_optimisation_practices.reader_description: Adipose biopsy trials have mixed results: some tissue endpoints improved, while another trial found no inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation. system_optimisation_practices.input: Ten-hour eating window for adults with obesity and long baseline eating windows

system_optimisation_practices.reader_description: A small trial supports this exact protocol, while the adipose analysis was exploratory and selected the greatest weight losers. A separate trial found no extra visceral-fat benefit from adding time restriction to Mediterranean-diet education.

lifestyle_priorities.biological_role: Exercise training changed adipocyte size, extracellular matrix and capillarization without weight loss in the assessed study.
lifestyle_priorities.evidence_limitation: Counterbalanced allocation between two exercise programmes, no sedentary control and several transient responses limit causal and durability claims.
lifestyle_priorities.reader_description: Regular training can alter adipose structure even without weight loss. The assessed comparison does not establish a general sustained anti-inflammatory effect or a superior training intensity.

lifestyle_priorities.reader_description: A controlled sleep-loss experiment increased visceral fat. Evidence for reversing established adipose inflammation by sleep extension remains a separate question.

scientific_principles.title: 11β-HSD1 cortisone–cortisol interconversion
scientific_principles.proposition: HSD11B1 catalyses NADP(H)-dependent cortisone–cortisol interconversion and predominantly acts as a reductase in vivo.
scientific_principles.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid regeneration; reaction participation of NADPH is distinct from a dietary requirement.
scientific_principles.scope_limitations: Molecular reaction identity does not establish its net rate in every tissue, dietary niacin limitation, or an optimal cortisol concentration.
scientific_principles.classification_rationale: Curated enzyme/reaction identity; context-dependent human regulation is assessed separately in SF13.

scientific_principles.title: Leptin and adiponectin are distinct endocrine molecules
scientific_principles.proposition: Leptin and adiponectin are distinct adipokines with receptor identities LEPR and ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2, respectively.
scientific_principles.mechanism: Adipose endocrine communication; production, release, circulating exposure and target responsiveness are separate relationships.
scientific_principles.scope_limitations: No claim that concentrations measure secretion or receptor sensitivity; no dietary or clinical effect follows from molecular identity.
scientific_principles.classification_rationale: Curated molecular and receptor relationships, not an intervention synthesis.
